study type: Secondary analysis of an observational obstetric cohort
exposure: Mode of operative delivery in the second stage of labor (vacuum, forceps, or cesarean delivery)
outcome: Composite neonatal outcome (death, fracture, length of stay ≥3 days beyond mother's, low Apgar, subgaleal hemorrhage, ventilator support, hypoxic encephalopathy, brachial plexus injury, facial nerve palsy)
cohort: 2,531 women with singleton pregnancies at ≥37 weeks gestation, nonanomalous, vertex presentation, no prior vaginal delivery, who reached a station of +2 or below and underwent an attempt at an operative delivery
finding: In patients needing second-stage delivery assistance with a station of +2 or below, attempted operative vaginal delivery was associated with a lower frequency of postpartum infection but a higher frequency of severe lacerations compared to cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Attempted operative vaginal delivery (vacuum or forceps) was associated with a lower frequency of postpartum infection compared to cesarean delivery.
